authoring_rules: Seventh held-out set, for the digest-grounded summary decision (README.md: arms BASE, V2, SRC, DIGEST).

Gold functions are drawn in the seeded order of draw.json (select.py), not picked; each drawn function gets one developer question it directly answers, or a recorded skip (trivial / unaskable / duplicate), until 30 questions per repository.
Written from the source at the pinned commits before any engine, search, ranking or summarizer ran on these repositories; only the name-only pool (select.py, check.py) was built.
Same rules as sets 1-6: developer phrasing; gold = the function(s) that directly answer; decoys = plausible wrong functions (a sibling, the caller or the callee, the inverse operation).
No question contains its gold symbol's name or every word of it (check.py).
Gold and decoys are library code in the pool, never test files; no property setter is gold or decoy.

questions.question: If the request body was already read into memory by an earlier call, where does form parsing get its bytes from so it does not read input that was already consumed?
Which request method can a subclass override to decide where each uploaded file's contents are buffered during multipart parsing?
How is a Set-Cookie value built: when is the value quoted with octal escapes, what turns Secure on automatically, and when is a warning about its size emitted?
While a form is parsed, are uploaded files kept in memory or written to a temporary file on disk, and what size threshold decides that?
How do I run a WSGI application against an environ and turn its output, status and headers into a response object, optionally buffering the whole body?
On a header collection, how do I read a header and, only when it is missing, store a fallback value and return that?
After changing a URL rule's attributes in place, what re-binds it to its map so its matching is rebuilt?
For a 429 or 503 error, how is the Retry-After header added to the response, and how is a datetime written differently from a number of seconds?
Right before a response starts, how is the Location header made absolute, Content-Length dropped for 1xx and 204, entity headers stripped for 304, and the length computed for buffered bodies?
In a dict that keeps several values per key, how do I remove a key and get all of its values back, receiving an empty list instead of an error when the key is absent?
How do I get an unbound copy of a URL rule so it can be reused in a different map?

How does deleting a header remove every value stored under that name regardless of letter case?

How do I replace a response body with a string or bytes, and when is the Content-Length header updated to match?

How can I plug in my own parser for the browser identification header on incoming requests?

After a failed URL build, how is each candidate rule weighed when suggesting the closest one: how much do endpoint-name similarity, the given arguments and the method count?

How does a client connection get handed back to the connector's pool for reuse once a response is finished?
How is a small WebSocket message compressed and written in one go without awaiting, including setting the RSV1 bit and stripping the deflate trailer?
Which middleware factory sends requests to a path with an added or removed trailing slash or merged double slashes, and in what order are those fixes tried?
Which client session method sends a request with the HTTP verb meant for submitting data, carrying a body?

How are HTTP basic credentials built out of the user and password embedded in an address like http://user:pass@host, and what if the address has neither?
